title: Odd Requests Signal Brief + Fast Probe Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
Quick, informal roll-up of low-frequency / high-friction customer asks we've seen May-July 2026. These are the 'weird but repeatable' signals that don't fit the main VOC themes (latency/cost/rollouts) but cause high churn or engineering churn on a per-customer basis. Goal: capture patterns, propose lightweight probes, and assign owners for 2-week fast experiments that either resolve or escalate to product backlog.

How to read this note:
- Tight: each signal has a one-line customer quote, 2–3 root hypotheses, and 1–2 low-effort probes we can run this sprint.
- Outcome: either close as 'probe resolved' with copy + template, or create an RFC ticket (tag: CS-EDGE) if it materially impacts platform behavior.

Signals observed (ordered by frequency x pain):
1) "Model variant mismatch in canary: customer says output tone changes across regions"
   - Quote: "We saw polite -> terse responses when traffic fell back from us-west to eu-central, broke our UX."
   - Hypotheses: routing policy selects different model variant (quantized/float mix) without clear version mapping; different default tokenization configs per region; cache warmup state (KV prefix) leads to style drift.
   - Fast probes:
     - Reproduce: create synthetic request stream with identical prompts hitting us-west and eu-central; capture model id, quantization tag, and RNG seed. (Owner: SRE test harness - Liam)
     - Customer-facing immediate action: template to recommend pinning exact model & quantization profile for critical routes; sample YAML and SDK snippet. (Owner: CS playbook - Maya)

2) "Requests for token-level cost breakdown tied to routes and embeddings"
   - Quote: "We need to show finance exactly which route produced these tokens; per-route cost variance is killing our forecasts."
   - Hypotheses: customers mix Hosted + Dedicated endpoints and want unified billing attribution; current Console only shows aggregate tokens by billing project, not by route/model pair.
   - Fast probes:
     - Dashboard patch mock: build a 1-page mockup showing route -> model -> tokens table and circulate to finance stakeholders (Owner: Product/Console - Priya).
     - Short-term workaround: provide CSV export script that annotates request_id -> route -> token_count, plus instructions to join with billing exports. (Owner: CS tooling - Diego)

3) "Embedding duplicates and version drift complaints from search teams"
   - Quote: "Two weeks later, search results are wildly different even though we didn't change prompts — embeddings aren't stable after a model micro-update."
   - Hypotheses: model patch changed embedding head; small quantization toggles matter for high-similarity workloads; no sticky versioning applied for embedding endpoints by customers.
   - Fast probes:
     - Run a stability matrix: compute cosine similarities for canonical dataset across three model snapshots available in catalog; publish a one-page risk table. (Owner: Applied ML liaison - Priya)
     - Customer mitigation: recommend pin to specific model sha + export reproducible embedding job with seed/params. Provide a canned script. (Owner: CS)

4) "Requests to expose KV-cache warmup metrics and cache hit patterns"
   - Quote: "We're seeing cold-start spikes for multi-turn sessions; ops asked for cache hit logs per session."
   - Hypotheses: cache warming happens at GPU-local layer and isn't surfaced; customers treat multi-turn as stateful app but platform treats most requests as stateless by default.
   - Fast probes:
     - Small SRE instrumentation: add ephemeral trace that tags requests with kv-cache-state: cold|partial|warm and expose as header in response for 2 weeks. Use opt-in query param. (Owner: Serving-runtime - Liam)
     - Customer guide: best practices for session affinity + template for sticky routing using our SDK. (Owner: CS)

5) "Edge-case privacy ask: per-model key wrapping and in-flight HSM pinning"
   - Quote: "Finance needs to ensure this inference run used customer-key A for model X and not a platform key."
   - Hypotheses: enterprise customers need auditable key usage per inference; our current Private offering supports KMS but not per-model key binding in a granular auditable way.
   - Fast probes:
     - Security feasibility review: pull in Sec/Compliance for 48h spike analysis and list gating constraints (HSM availability, perf hit). (Owner: Security - Diego)
     - Triage note to Enterprise PM: collect top-3 customers with that ask and size as small incremental product item. (Owner: CS)

Operational patterns and churn drivers we've noticed:
- Many 'odd' asks are caused by customers not pinning model+quantization+tokenizer together. When the catalog auto-updates, tiny changes surface as major regressions for specialized workloads (search, legal summarization).
- Console visibility gaps (per-route token exports, cache state, model variant tags) increase support time by ~2–4 hrs per incident.
- Customers with dedicated pools expect deterministic behavior; any fallback to hosted variants is perceived as a bug even when documented.

Suggested short-term playbook (2-week cadence):
- Week 0: run probes above in parallel; produce 1-page reproducible artifact for each signal (repro script + sample CSV + recommended mitigation).
- Week 1: run customer syncs for top-2 affected accounts, provide tailored mitigation and collect acceptance criteria.
- Week 2: either close probe (ship quick docs + SDK snippet) or open Product RFC with quantifiable user impact and proposed changes.

Customer templates to ship quickly (samples included in attachments):
- Pin-model YAML snippet for SDK with explicit quantization and tokenizer fields.
- CSV export join example: billing_export_id -> request_id -> route_tag -> token_count. SQL query sample for finance teams.
- Sticky-session SDK example with retry policy and response header check to detect kv-cache warm state.

Unresolved questions / flags for PMs:
- Do we want an official 'pin and freeze' API for customers who need absolute behavior guarantees across regions? Possible product, but asks bandwidth + compliance work.
- How to balance exposing low-level runtime signals (cache state, quantization tag) vs. exposing internal implementation details that increase surface area for confusion?

Immediate next steps (owners + due dates):
- Liam: run region mismatch repro harness (due: 2026-07-22).
- Priya: mock Console page and circulate to 3 customers for feedback (due: 2026-07-23).
- Diego: open security spike doc for per-model key audit (due: 2026-07-21).
- Maya (CS): craft three customer email templates (pin model, CSV billing join, session affinity) and add to playbook repo (due: 2026-07-20).

Appendix: quick logs and snippets (raw notes)
- Raw customer snippet A: "Our AI output changed tone after a weekend — we didn't change code."
- Quick SQL (billing join): SELECT r.request_id, r.route, b.tokens FROM requests r JOIN billing b ON r.request_id=b.request_id WHERE r.project='acct-123';
- SDK pin snippet (pseudo): client.generate({model: 'rwd-embed-v2@sha:0abc', quantization: 'q4_0', tokenizer: 'v2', request_id: '...'});

Closing note:
This is intentionally lightweight and operational — not a final product spec. If a probe repeatedly surfaces the same tradeoff (determinism vs auto-rollout), escalate to Product with a clear customer impact metric (e.g., number of incidents avoided per quarter).

If you want a one-hour walkthrough of any of the probes, ping me and I'll run through the reproducible notebook live.

-- Maya
